defects_found_beyond_the_contract: test_calendar_interop had a SECOND, SEPARATE break: it used CanonicalArgusDriver::bind, which installs its OWN app-data root. Inside the Argus window the mounted app emitter resolved a binding the fixture-owned backend could not see, so every automatic native-editor event emitted there 401d and wait_for_calendar_fr reported a NON-EXISTENT product defect. Fixed with bind_in_current_app_data carrying the same token, and argus.finish() moved AFTER the zero-residue cleanup because it drops the SwarmMcpServer and deletes the binding.

FOUR mounted stub-server proofs in the same suite were measuring nothing. One (mounted_activity_404_and_503_preserve_event_without_activity_fr) asserted a POSITIVE FR post and failed deterministically because the emitter fails closed without a binding. THREE others asserted native_fr_posts == 0 VACUOUSLY, since the emitter aborts before ever reaching the socket. All four now publish a real binding, so the negative assertions finally measure product behaviour instead of measuring the missing credential.

pt_115_3_blocker_requiring_operator_deci.finding: The document_saved attribution clause is UNSATISFIABLE BY THE REAL PRODUCT. validate_document_save_receipt requires row.actor_id == event.canonical_actor_id() (src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/flight_recorder.rs, VERIFIED AT THAT LINE BY KERNEL_BUILDER). The recorder actor is server-derived as handshake-native:{pid}:{birth_fingerprint} by capture_context, while POST/PUT /knowledge/documents... has NO session authentication at all and takes its actor from a client header (backend_client::DOC_ACTOR_ID = handshake-native-editor). No route exposes the derived identity, so the frontend cannot stamp it.
pt_115_3_blocker_requiring_operator_deci.evidence_chain: Real product save then document_saved ingestion with a genuine session token and every payload field matching the ledger row => HTTP 400 HSK-400-INVALID-EVENT. SAME authenticated session, same workspace, undo_fired => HTTP 200 with actor_id handshake-native:13496:66b7100f. Ledger row for the save receipt carries actor_id=handshake-native-editor. DECISIVE POSITIVE CONTROL: re-running with the document save issued under x-hsk-actor-id set to the server-derived native actor makes document_saved ingestion return HTTP 200. A temporary probe was used and then deleted.
pt_115_3_blocker_requiring_operator_deci.why_it_matters: MT-109 stated intent is that a save receipt can only be claimed by the principal that minted it. That requires BOTH endpoints to authenticate the same principal. Today only one does, so the clause does not enforce the invariant - it rejects EVERYTHING legitimate. A guard that always fails is not a security control; it is an outage that looks like one.
pt_115_3_blocker_requiring_operator_deci.why_not_fixed_here: Every fix inside MT-115 allowed_paths would WEAKEN the binding. The non-weakening fix - authenticate the document-save route from the native session, or expose the derived identity through a route the frontend can use - lives in api/knowledge_documents.rs or a new route, outside allowed_paths, and is a durable security-contract decision. Routed to MT-120 rather than decided unilaterally.

palmistry_forwarder_resolved_with_a_thir.what_was_found: FR_ROUTE_PATH named /api/flight_recorder/runtime_chat_event, which MT-109 deleted. Beyond the two reasons the contract listed, the agent verified a THIRD and decisive one in source: capture_context requires process_birth_identity(binding.pid) to STILL MATCH, i.e. the app process must be ALIVE. Palmistry exists precisely to survive a freeze or crash, so at the exact moment it has evidence worth forwarding, even reading the app binding file yields StaleBinding => 401.
palmistry_forwarder_resolved_with_a_thir.consequence: Option (a) "just add the credential" is not a small change: it requires a NEW out-of-process principal class able to write attributed FR rows while the app is dead - and it still has no workspace.
palmistry_forwarder_resolved_with_a_thir.implemented: Option (c): removed the dead constant (not renamed, not re-pointed), made the ingestion path an explicit constructor argument, and production binds None. Production behaviour is BYTE-IDENTICAL - SchemaIncompatible still short-circuits before any network call. Two new tests pin it. Palmistry lib 77/77, test_fr_forward 6/6, test_end_to_end_support 5/5, test_survivor_store 7/7, exit 0.
palmistry_forwarder_resolved_with_a_thir.recommendation_for_the_operator: Keep the deferral, and when WP-KERNEL-016 opens it prefer (b) a SEPARATE INGESTION BOUNDARY over (a): a survivor-intake route with its own capability and credential shape, because the FR group credential is process-liveness-bound BY DESIGN and Palmistry is defined by outliving that process. Confirming the deferral in .GOV is the operator call; the agent did not touch .GOV.

scope.summary: Close the remaining MT-109 authorization fallout: the Palmistry forwarder design question, the seven test harnesses that still read the recorder without a credential, and document_saved actor attribution.

part_1_palmistry.problem: src/frontend/palmistry/fr_forward.rs:52 FR_ROUTE_PATH still names the REMOVED unscoped /api/flight_recorder/runtime_chat_event. The constant is now dead.
part_1_palmistry.why_not_a_rename: Palmistry is an OUT-OF-PROCESS watcher whose entire purpose is surviving Handshake freezes and crashes. It has NO workspace id and NO native-MCP binding, so it can satisfy NEITHER half of the new contract (workspace-scoped path + session token). This is a genuine design question, not a mechanical fix.
part_1_palmistry.options_for_the_authority_owner: Either (a) give Palmistry a distinct capability and an out-of-process credential path appropriate to a watcher that must work when the app is dead, or (b) route Palmistry forwarding through a different ingestion boundary entirely, or (c) formally confirm the existing typed SchemaIncompatible deferral to WP-KERNEL-016 and REMOVE the dead constant so no future reader believes the route still exists.
part_1_palmistry.current_safety: It already returns a typed SchemaIncompatible blocker, so nothing regressed into silence.

part_2_test_harness_credentials.problem: Seven suites still read the Flight Recorder with NO credential and will 401 under the MT-109 gate: test_calendar_interop (4 sites), test_ckc_embed (1), test_e7_swarm_edit_proof (1), test_fems_interop_proofs (5 of 7), test_locus_interop (1), test_other_pillar_interop_proofs (6), test_code_note_cross_ref (2, stub server).

MT-027 and MT-066 independently proved the same publish-a-real-binding pattern.
part_2_test_harness_credentials.requirement: Each suite needs RealNativeMcpBinding::publish() BEFORE its backend selection; the ordering is suite-specific. Under NO circumstances weaken, stub, feature-gate or bypass the authorization to make a suite green - present a genuine binding or report a blocking gap.
